default_exit._why: one exit for every family so rules compete on the same footing; the owner will decide the demo stop/take-profit later and this block changes then (a change = a new screen run, its variants counted again)
default_exit._fills: signal at the close of bar t; market order at the open of the 1-minute bar that starts at t's close (+ slippage); every 1-minute bar from the entry minute on: stop first (fills at the stop or the gap open, - slippage), then the target (a limit: needs a trade 1 tick through, fills at the target); time exit at the open of the first minute at or after entry + max_hold_min; flat at the session's flatten time; one position at a time; at most max_entries_per_session entries per session

E-728.title: Open-dwell share dip entry
E-728.hypothesis: When most of the session's bars closed on one side of the day open, the day is a one-sided auction; a dip through a short EMA that closes back on the dominant side is cheap continuation for the trend participants.

E-729.title: Early-extreme survival VWAP cross
E-729.hypothesis: If the day's high (low) formed early and the opposite extreme formed later, the day is a trend day; after the morning, a close through VWAP in the trend direction means trapped early buyers (sellers) give up.

E-730.title: VWAP cross confirmed by the other market's side
E-730.hypothesis: A cross of the own VWAP is more reliable when the other contract (usually negatively correlated) sits on its opposite side of its short EMA: both markets then express the same risk flow.

E-731.title: Day-range position divergence versus the other market
E-731.hypothesis: Index and dollar usually share inverse range positions inside the day. When the index sits far lower in its day range than the dollar implies, the laggard converges.

E-732.title: Up-bar versus down-bar range balance follow
E-732.hypothesis: When the range printed by up bars dominates the range printed by down bars over a window, buyers cause the wider moves and the imbalance persists.

E-733.title: Higher-high versus lower-low frequency balance
E-733.hypothesis: A window with many bars making higher highs and few making lower lows shows one side continually extending the price; the first time the balance gets lopsided marks control.

E-734.title: V-turn after a sharp opposite move
E-734.hypothesis: A large move in the opposite direction of the one just before it, both beyond what is typical, signals that the earlier side was absorbed; follow the turn.

E-735.title: Busy-volume pace with VWAP and open side
E-735.hypothesis: When cumulative session volume runs well ahead of its typical pace, participation is unusually high; price on the same side of VWAP and day open carries conviction that persists.

E-736.title: Mid-range recovery measured in average daily range
E-736.hypothesis: Price that sits at least a fraction of the typical daily range away from both session extremes is in the middle of an expanded day; the VWAP side then gives the continuation direction.

E-737.title: Volume-peak bar failure
E-737.hypothesis: The highest-volume bar of a window shows where aggressive participants committed; a close beyond the extreme of that bar against its direction traps them and forces exits.
